children: The cost ‌of shipping oil in supertankers surged to fresh record highs this week, Bloomberg reported, following the biggest wave of attacks on Middle East shipping since the start of the U.S.-Iran war.

Earnings for Very Large Crude Carriers sailing on the benchmark Middle East-to-China route reportedly hit a record of nearly $800K/day, while the U.S. Gulf-to-Asia run has fetched offers at a record lump-sum fee of $29.5M, nearly $15/bbl without considering additional war risks or fees for unexpected delays.
The Baltic Exchange, which has begun publishing an index to cover the voyage from the Gulf of Oman to east Asia, estimates daily earnings on the route have spiked 85% to nearly $386K/day this week.

VLCC freight rates for the Middle East to Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp route also spiked to a fresh high, and the Middle East's military ​escalation had a ​wider knock-on effect, as rates on the West Africa to Asia route also reached a record ​high, according to a Reuters report that cited Baltic Exchange data.
Freight analysis from data intelligence firm Kpler suggests dayrates for VLCCs will stay above $100K into next year, more than double historic levels that rarely went above $45K.
"There's quite a few bottlenecks all at the same time," Equinor's

global head of crude, products and liquids trading Alex Grant told Bloomberg at the Asia Pacific Petroleum Conference by S&P Global Energy in Singapore. "The market is quite stressed with all of that, and that's showing up in the shipping rates."

Freight costs have reacted much more sharply than oil prices to the global disruptions, as the U.S. and Iran hit tankers in the Persian Gulf, Houthi militants are ramping up attacks in the Red Sea, and Ukraine strikes Russian oil infrastructure and product exports.
If elevated shipping costs persist, they ​could add to inflationary pressures and further raise costs for businesses and ​consumers.

title: Oil tanker rates reach record highs on surging risks to Middle East shipping
